items.title: Photo of litter sparks anger among Mississauga residents
items.summary: A social media post reminding residents to pick up litter garnered over 800 comments—but the photo wasn’t actually from the weekend. The City of Mississauga posted a photo of a large amount of garbage left behind in a picnic shelter. “Long weekends should leave memories, not garbage,” the Aug. 4 post reads. “Every year, litter and illegally dumped waste are left behind in parks and green spaces. ​” The post on Facebook had over 800 comments by Wednesday. “Send the bill to the person that booked that spot,” one person said. “Can we not just take our own garbage home???? That’s what I would have done,” another said. com. “It was not issued in response to a specific littering or illegal dumping incident from the weekend,” the spokesperson said.

items.title: Outdoor movie nights return to the City Centre in Mississauga
items.summary: An animated crime comedy film that’s sure to deliver laughs gets things started on Thursday evening as the hugely popular Celebration Square Movie Nights return for another summer at the downtown Mississauga venue. The gang gets back together to pull off one last heist in The Bad Guys 2 and all the action can be seen on the big screen at Celebration Square. The 2025 American film produced by DreamWorks Animation kicks off this summer’s five-film series that’ll entertain outdoor Mississauga audiences throughout the rest of the summer on Thursday nights (see full movie listings below). com, are scheduled each week starting this Thursday, Aug. 6, with The Bad Guys 2 and continuing until Sept. 3, the City of Mississauga said in an online event update. Stop by the INsauga photo booth at every movie, strike a pose, and test your movie knowledge for a chance to win fun trivia prizes. What city officials describe as the largest outdoor movie screenings in Mississauga are open to all ages, admission is free and the venue is accessible. m. Launching the 2026 outdoor movie season at Celebration Square, The Bad Guys 2 — sequel to The Bad Guys (2022) — follows the story of, who else, the Bad Guys, who are forced to come out of retirement and join forces with an all-female criminal squad to perform one last heist. The second film in the franchise stars Sam Rockwell, Marc Maron, Awkwafina, Craig Robinson, Anthony Ramos, Zazie Beetz, Alex Borstein, Richard Ayoade and Lilly Singh reprising their roles from the first film. Danielle Brooks, Natasha Lyonne and Maria Bakalova join the cast in the latest movie. Movie night organizers urge residents to forget the traditional indoor movie theatre for a while — at least one night a week — and instead grab a blanket and watch some popular films under the stars in the heart of Mississauga’s City Centre.

items.title: Mississauga reminds residents about Balcony Basics for balcony and window safety
items.summary: Simple steps can help prevent serious injuries. Emergency and public safety | August 5, 2026 Balcony Basics reminds residents that balcony and window safety is a shared responsibility. Falls from windows and balconies can cause serious injuries or death, but many incidents can be prevented through simple safety precautions and increased awareness. Common hazards include furniture placed near windows or balcony railings, unsecured windows and window screens that are not designed to prevent falls. Young children face the greatest risk, while older adults may be more vulnerable due to mobility or balance challenges. Renters and highrise residents should also know how to spot hazards and take action. Keeping apartments and highrise buildings safe is a shared responsibility. Balcony and window safety requires action from everyone involved. Residents, renters, landlords, parents, caregivers and seniors all play an important role in preventing injuries. They can report concerns early. Property owners, landlords and building managers are responsible for keeping safety features in good working order. They must respond quickly when issues are identified. The City supports safety through education, inspections and enforcement actions to help prevent injuries before they occur.

items.title: Peel's Colour-Coded Health Inspection System Just Played Out at a Mississauga Restaurant
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Public Health records show that Charminar Indian Cuisine on Spectrum Way in Mississauga received a red card during an inspection on July 31, the most serious rating the agency issues. Inspectors found what the report describes as a significant risk of possible contamination or adulteration at the restaurant, serious enough to trigger an immediate closure. INsauga explains that a red card means an inspector found an actual health risk or danger, and under Peel's system that forces the establishment to close until the problem is fixed. Charminar has since been reinspected and given a green passing grade, allowing the restaurant to reopen. The outlet also notes the distinction with a yellow card, which signals a conditional pass where the establishment isn't fully meeting requirements under the Health Protection and Promotion Act but can keep operating while it fixes the issues. For Charminar's customers, the sequence shows how quickly a serious violation can shut a kitchen down, and how a passed reinspection gets it back open just as fast.

items.title: After 80 Years, Canada Will Import the Base Oils a Mississauga Refinery Used to Make
items.summary: According to INsauga, HF Sinclair will end more than 80 years of base oil production at its Mississauga waterfront refinery once it retires the site's refining assets, ending Canada's largest source of these industrial oils. Base oils are the primary ingredient in lubricants such as motor oils, transmission fluids, hydraulic fluids and other industrial products used across the country and beyond. INsauga reports HF Sinclair has now answered the question of how it will keep supplying customers once local production stops. Chevron Products Company will supply Group II base oils and South Korea-based SK Enmove will supply Group III base oils, replacing what used to be made on site in Mississauga. The outlet describes it as a major shift away from a Canadian manufacturing model toward one built on imports from overseas suppliers. For a facility that has anchored Mississauga's waterfront industrial base for eight decades, the move marks the end of local production for a major category of oils that have been manufactured there for generations.

items.title: Developer Behind Mississauga's First Proposed AI Data Centre Signals It Will Fight the New Building Freeze
items.summary: According to the Kenora Miner & News, Mississauga council voted Wednesday to pause approvals for new data centre developments for at least twelve months, following more than five hours of debate and over 20 delegations from residents. The freeze grew out of concerns raised a month earlier at a packed town hall over the city's first proposed AI data centre, a roughly 220,015-square-foot facility that real estate firm Prologis wants to build at the northwest corner of Tenth Line West and Argentia Road. Residents pressed council on the project's water use, its draw on the electricity grid, air and noise pollution, and how densely computing hardware would be packed into the building, questions officials acknowledged they still don't have full answers to. Prologis had already worked through the city's Committee of Adjustment and Planning and Development Committee, where staff found the proposal generally consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and the Mississauga Official Plan. Despite that earlier progress, the outlet reports the company is expected to challenge council's new pause. The vote makes Mississauga the only municipality in Ontario to freeze new data centre approvals so far.

items.title: North America's Only Multilingual Fringe Festival Returns to Mississauga With 48 Shows Across Two Weeks
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, SAWITRI Theatre Group is running the sixth edition of the Mississauga Multilingual Fringe Festival this month, an event the organization describes as the only multilingual fringe festival in North America. This year's lineup includes 48 performances across 12 different productions staged in English, Hindi, Urdu, Punjabi and other languages over two weeks. The first week of shows runs from August 10 to 16 at AN1 Studios, followed by a second week from August 17 to 23 at Sampradaya Theatre. Beyond the stage performances, the festival includes a visual arts exhibition featuring graphic design, oil painting and prints, plus a singing competition called Sing Under the Stars on August 22 with a cash prize on the line. SAWITRI Theatre Group was founded in 2003 by Artistic Co-Directors Jasmine Sawant and Shruti Shah and has since won the 2016 Marty's Award for excellence in theatre. Modern Mississauga Media notes the company runs three festivals a year in total, with the Multilingual Fringe Festival built around its mandate to spotlight South Asian theatre, women's stories and socio-political themes across multiple languages.
